newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CULLINAN BOOSTS S.AFRICA IN TRIANGULAR FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CULLINAN BOOSTS S.AFRICA IN TRIANGULAR FINAL.

text.p: Daryll Cullinan stroked 60 from 51 balls as South Africa scored a challenging 278 for eight off 50 overs against India in the re-played triangular series final on Thursday.
South Africa, unbeaten in the tournament from which Zimbabwe were eliminated, threatened a total in excess of 300 with six overs remaining.
But seamer Venkatesh Prasad took two wickets in consecutive deliveries in the 44th over to check South Africa's momentum, five wickets falling for 45 as they slipped to 266 for eight at one stage.
After South African captain Hansie Cronje won his first toss of the tournament, the home side took full advantage of a good batting pitch at Kingsmead.
Openers Gary Kirsten (51) and Andrew Hudson (19) built a solid foundation with a confident stand of 44 in 11 overs under leaden skies.
Although Hudson was then given out caught behind off fast bowler Javagal Srinath, Kirsten and Jacques Kallis (49) lifted the tempo with a second-wicket partnership of 86 in 92 balls.
Kirsten, having reached his fourth 50 of the triangular series from 65 deliveries, was caught in the deep attempting a pull-sweep off all-rounder Robin Singh.
Kallis departed to the next ball, leg before as he drove at Singh.
However, Cullinan and Jonty Rhodes (41) took the innings to new heights as they pushed the run rate to 5.9 per over with an exhilarating stand of 91 in 81 balls.
The original final had to be abandoned without a result on Wednesday because of rain.
